source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Fuel - Air Cleaners, p.6M-11

procedures.title: Air cleaner: maintenance intervals
steps: Turn the oiled paper element 180° at 12,000 miles.
Do both more often in dusty or other harsh driving conditions.
notes: 1968 Chevrolets use 3 types: oiled paper, oiled paper with polyurethane band, and wire mesh with polyurethane band.
Light discoloration of an oiled paper element from a little dirt does not mean it is plugged or less effective.
Most automatic transmission cars have a thermostatic inlet air temperature control that mixes heat stove air and under-hood air.

procedures.title: Polyurethane air cleaner element: clean
steps: Remove the cover wing nut, cover and element.
Check the element for tears or rips and replace it if needed.
Clean all dirt from the air cleaner bottom and cover; discard the air horn gaskets.
Take the element off its support screen, wash it in kerosene or mineral spirits and squeeze out the solvent (see figure 3A in the manual); never use hot degreaser or acetone-type solvents.
Dip the element in light engine oil and squeeze out the excess.
